subtitle: Three-Engine Parallel Reverb
tagline: Three reverb engines, Glue, Bright, and Space, run side by side. Each has its own send, character, filters, and solo, and all three meet at one WET / DRY control.
facts: Room, Chamber, Plate, Spring, Hall, IR

body.lead: A single reverb algorithm usually forces a compromise between closeness, colour, and long depth. TB Parallel Reverb runs three independent reverb engines in parallel, so each spatial role can be tuned and auditioned on its own before the final blend.

body.p: Glue adds short room or chamber body. Bright adds plate or spring character. Space adds a long hall or a loaded impulse response. Each engine has its own send, pre-delay, width, decay, filters, and colour, and you can solo any engine while you tune it. Because the engines are independent, one can change without forcing the others to follow the same decay or colour.

ul: Three parallel engines: Glue (Room, Chamber), Bright (Plate, Spring), and Space (Hall, IR)
Per-engine SEND, PRE-DELAY, WIDE, DECAY, DIFFUSION, LOW CUT, HIGH CUT, and COLOR

Four hall types and impulse response loading (WAV, AIFF, FLAC) in the Space engine
ON / OFF and SOLO footswitches on each pedal, with an ENGINE STATE overview
99 factory presets in ten banks, plus user presets

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Parallel Reverb 3.1.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is version 1.0.4 and may differ from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert TB Parallel Reverb on an aux (send) track and leave `WET / DRY` {{12}} at its default of 100%, which outputs only the reverb. On an insert, lower `WET / DRY` to blend the reverb with the dry sound.
Choose a factory preset from the preset bar {{1}} that matches your source, or start from the defaults.
Press `SOLO` {{11}} on one pedal to hear that engine alone. Set its `SEND`, `DECAY`, and filters {{4}} {{6}}.
Repeat for the other engines. Switch off any engine you do not need with its `ON / OFF` footswitch {{10}}.
Turn solo off and balance the three `SEND` levels in the mix.

tip.text: Send Gain sets each engine's own return level; WET / DRY sets the overall relationship between the source and the summed reverb. Balance the sends first, then set WET / DRY.

body.p: Step through the factory presets with the arrows in the preset bar {{1}}, or open the PRESET list. LOAD USER PRESET... opens a .tbprpreset file, and Save stores the current settings as one. The name shows CUSTOM after you change a preset. Undo and Redo step through recent changes.

body.p: Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Vocal depth without mud
recipes.use: A lead vocal that stays forward with space behind it.
settings: Lead Vocal Forward or Vocal Plate Halo
steps: Solo each engine and cut the lows until the return stops clouding the voice.
Keep Space low in the send so the tail sits behind the vocal.

recipes.title: Drum room plus plate
recipes.use: Body from a room and snap from a plate.
steps: Switch Space off with ON / OFF.
Raise Glue SEND until the kit sounds like one room.

recipes.title: Ambient wash
recipes.use: Long, soft tails for pads and atmospheres.
steps: Lower HIGH CUT on Space if the tail gets bright and busy.

recipes.title: Real space with an IR
recipes.use: Place a source in a recorded room or hall.
steps: Load a WAV, AIFF, or FLAC impulse response.
Shape it with LENGTH, LOW CUT, and HIGH CUT.

rows: WET / DRY is at 100%, the default for aux use. Lower it on an insert.
I cannot hear the dry sound or the other engines.
An engine is soloed. Turn SOLO off before you export.
Raise LOW CUT on each engine, starting with Space.
The reverb is harsh or splashy.
Lower HIGH CUT or COLOR, or raise DAMPING (Glue) or HF DAMPING (Space).
No impulse response is loaded (NO IR SELECTED). Load one with BROWSE IR...
Lower WIDE on the engines and check again in mono.
Switch off engines you are not using.

body.p: The path of the loaded impulse response is stored with the plug-in state rather than as a host parameter. If you move the file, load it again with BROWSE IR...
